//automation: Automation shared by every desk. A folder means one file per event (recommended)
//tab_bar_width: Width of the tab bar on the left, in pixels. Leave it out for the default. Dragging its edge on screen changes it too, and writes the new value back here. 0 puts the tab bar away (so does Ctrl+B s)
//side_bar_width: Width of the panel on the right, in pixels. 0 or left out keeps it put away. Dragging its edge on screen changes it too, and writes the new value back here (Ctrl+B g shows and hides it)
//secrets: Slack, Discord and Telegram tokens do not go here -- they go in the secrets file (never share it)
//remote: The remote UI, for watching and giving instructions from a phone or another device. Off unless enabled. bind: auto (Tailscale, then LAN) is recommended
//keys: Key bindings. Write the key against the name of the action, not the action against the key. A key with a modifier (ctrl+shift+d) works on its own; a single character (z) works after the prefix key. off gives a key up. The list of action names is under Keys in the settings screen
//appearance: How the terminal looks. An empty font means the default (a pairing in which box-drawing characters and CJK text each fit their cells). font_size can also be changed with Ctrl+wheel over the terminal, and the value is written back here
//appearance.theme: The name of a color scheme, chosen from the list in the settings screen (the schemes Windows Terminal has on this PC, scheme files placed in config/themes, and the built-in ones). Colors can also be written out directly: {"background":"#1e1e2e","red":"#f38ba8", ...}
//external_api: A named pipe for driving the app from outside. children = only processes this app started (default) / user = anything running with your permissions (the passphrase is written to data/api-token) / off = no pipe
//desks: What you switch between. Either point at a definition file with file, or write the tabs in place
